title: AI-Part2: Setup-Vscode-al-copilot-business-central
summary: Setting up Visual Studio Code, the AL Language extension, and GitHub Copilot for Business Central AL development requires installation of three components and verification of connections. This post guides developers through each setup step and highlights common gotchas like extension version mismatches and separate subscription management.
key_points: Install VS Code as the only Microsoft-supported IDE for AL development, then add the AL Language extension from either the Marketplace or your BC container version
Run the AL: Go! command to create project structure, connect to your BC tenant, and download necessary symbols for standard BC objects
GitHub Copilot requires a separate subscription from both BC licenses and VS Code, so verify the subscription is active during extension installation
Test the full setup by publishing the sample AL file to your sandbox and running /explain commands in Copilot Chat to confirm all components communicate
Disable telemetry in VS Code settings if data privacy is a concern

quotes.text: Microsoft recommends pulling the AL Language extension version that ships directly from that container, rather than the Marketplace version, to avoid compiler-version mismatches
quotes.why_it_matters: Provides critical guidance on selecting the correct extension version to prevent compilation errors in specific BC environments
